packs.title: Parks and Spree
packs.promise: Find a different scale of Berlin in western gardens, southern open space and the eastern river.

q.s: Invent a small composition from formal and wandering paths.
st: From a stopped visitor path, find a straight garden edge and a softer curved edge. You can use the SPSG garden photograph instead.
On your own paper or device, make an original two-line composition: give one line most of the space and let the other interrupt it.
Add a short title of your own and save the drawing or describe its two lines in words.

q.s: Try two comfortable ways of reading an open path.
st: Choose a short comfortable stretch of open paved path. Stay out of the way of cyclists and skaters, and pick a point where you can stop safely.
Move at your usual comfortable pace, then stop and notice a distant shape. Make a second short passage at a slower comfortable pace, or compare the two views while stationary.
Write what the slower look changed. Turn back whenever you choose; there is no required lap, speed or distance.

q.s: Turn a lively facade into an original tiny verse.
st: From one stopped public position, choose a facade detail, a street sound and a movement that you notice. Describe them without identifying strangers.
Write an original six-word line that combines two of your observations. You can use the official street photograph if you prefer.
Change one word to give the line a different rhythm, then save the version you like.

packs.title: Read the Open City
packs.promise: Make your own reading of Berlin through shapes, streets, and water.

q.s: Collect the spaces inside a familiar outline.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Pariser Platz public square, east side of Brandenburg Gate. Keep the route through the space clear.
From a comfortable square-side viewpoint, find a vertical gap between columns, a horizontal band of stone, and a patch of sky around the rooftop sculpture.
Choose the space that changes most when you shift your gaze. Describe why it catches your attention without needing a full crossing.
Save your three spaces and a sentence about the one you chose.

q.s: Turn one short stretch of street into a sequence.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Unter den Linden public sidewalk from Pariser Platz toward Wilhelmstraße. Keep the route through the space clear.
Choose the open sidewalk on one side of this short stretch. Walk or roll a comfortable distance, using marked crossings only if needed; no fixed distance is required.
Notice three beats in order: a repeated tree or lamp, a building edge, and a change in light or street sound. If you prefer, use visual movement instead of sound.
Save the three beats in sequence as words or an optional photo with a note.

q.s: Make a skyline study in three marks or three lines.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Lustgarten public path facing Berliner Dom exterior. Keep the route through the space clear.
Look at the cathedral from outside its entrances. Choose a rounded roof shape, a vertical line, and a small area of sky.
Make a three-mark sketch or write three short lines that preserve those proportions. Give your study a title based on the light you see.
Save the study and its title, with an optional exterior photo.
